subject: Batched workload SLA split & credit-tiering proposal
messages:
From: Mark Chen <mark.chen@skylinefinance.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@skylinefinance.com
Date: Wed, 1 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: SLA split for batched inference workloads

Camila —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We like Redwood’s latency on short-chat flows, but our overnight portfolio scoring runs are batch-heavy and have different constraints. Our legal team asked if Redwood will accept a split in the SLA: 99.9% uptime for interactive/streaming endpoints and 99.5% for scheduled batch endpoints, with a pro-rated credit approach tied to the affected tokens during batch windows.

Two specific asks from Skyline:
- Limit the monthly service credit exposure to a hard cap of 8% of our monthly bill for batch-related incidents.
- Exclude scheduled batch maintenance windows up to 6 hours per month from uptime calculations, provided we receive 72 hours’ notice.

I attached a short PDF summarizing the asks (Skyline_SLA_Request.pdf) and an example credit calculation. Can Redwood confirm whether this is something you can accept as a contractual exception? If not, what alternatives would you propose?

-Mark Chen
Head of Platform Engineering
Skyline Finance
[Attachment: Skyline_SLA_Request.pdf (pdf)]

From: camila_reyes@redwood.com
To: Mark Chen <mark.chen@skylinefinance.com>
Cc: contracts@skylinefinance.com
Date: Wed, 1 Jul 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: SLA split for batched inference workloads

Mark —

Appreciate the note and the clear asks. We can explore a split SLA but want to balance operational predictability for both sides. Quick thoughts:

- Hard cap on credits: we typically offer a monthly cap tied to a percentage of monthly fees; 8% is within range but on the higher side for open-hosted tiers. For a committed reserved capacity arrangement we could accept a 10% cap, but for hosted customers we usually cap at 5–7%.
- Maintenance carveout: 72 hours’ notice is workable; our standard is 48 hours for planned maintenance but we can stretch to 72 for scheduled batch windows if Skyline provides a monthly calendar of expected windows.
- Latency vs uptime: easier if we treat batch endpoints as a separate route in the contract (so metrics are isolated). Pro-rated credits tied to affected tokens is plausible — we’ll need to agree on measurement definitions (what counts as a batch token, how to apportion cross-traffic).

I’ve looped in Logan (product) and Laura (legal) to weigh in on measurement and contract language. I can propose a concrete counterproposal by Friday if that timeline works.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.com
[Attachment referenced: proposed-credit-matrix.xlsx (will send)]

From: logan_wright@redwood.com
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com, Mark Chen <mark.chen@skylinefinance.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 2 Jul 2026 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA split for batched inference workloads

Hi Camila / Mark —

Thanks for the context. From a product/operational POV a few constraints to flag:

1) Measurement: We can report per-route availability and per-route token counts, but we need the batch routes to be explicitly configured (separate model alias or route path). For mixed routes we’ll default to the most conservative metric.

2) Credit calc: Pro-rating by token during the incident window is implementable, but will add complexity to monthly reconciliation and may require a small integration (we export a token-time-series CSV for each billing period).

3) Scheduled windows: We already schedule rolling infra maintenance. Carving out up to 6 hrs/mo is feasible if Skyline commits to the monthly calendar and doesn’t request dynamic shift without notice.

Suggested compromise we can diagram into the contract:
- Interactive endpoints: 99.9% monthly uptime SLO.
- Batch endpoints: 99.7% monthly uptime SLO (middle ground).
- Monthly credit cap: 10% of monthly fees for customers on a Dedicated plan; 6% cap for hosted (self-serve) customers.
- Credits for batch-related incidents: pro-rated by affected token counts; Redwood will provide a CSV export for reconciliation.

If that looks reasonable, Laura can draft the exception language and I’ll flag any operational dependencies for onboarding.

—Logan
Product Lead, Serving Runtime
[Sent from my desk — brief note to keep the thread moving]

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com, logan_wright@redwood.com, Mark Chen <mark.chen@skylinefinance.com>
Cc: contracts@skylinefinance.com
Date: Fri, 3 Jul 2026 09:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA split for batched inference workloads

Mark / Camila —

I reviewed the proposal. A couple of legal points to clarify before we lock language:

- Definitions: We must define "batch endpoints" and the measurement boundary (route name, model alias). The contract should require the customer to configure and declare which routes are batch.
- Notice & calendar: 72 hours’ notice for scheduled maintenance is acceptable only if the calendar is shared 30 days in advance and changes are limited to one revision per month.
- Caps & remedies: We can accept a differentiated cap (10% dedicated / 6% hosted) but want a clause that limits retroactive billing adjustments if the reconciliation CSVs show measurement disputes — i.e., a 30-day dispute window after which undisputed credits apply.

I’ll prepare a redline for the SLA section with those clauses; Camila, would you like me to put the 99.7% batch figure in the draft or leave it as a variable to negotiate?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Contracts Counsel
Redwood Inference

From: camila_reyes@redwood.com
To: Mark Chen <mark.chen@skylinefinance.com>, contracts@skylinefinance.com
Cc: logan_wright@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 6 Jul 2026 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA split for batched inference workloads

Mark —

Quick summary of where we landed internally and a proposed next step:

- Proposal we can offer (formal draft to follow):
  * Interactive SLO: 99.9% monthly uptime.
  * Batch SLO: 99.7% monthly uptime (applies only to routes declared as "batch" in onboarding).
  * Monthly credit cap: 10% for Dedicated customers (recommended for Skyline), 6% for hosted customers.
  * Maintenance carveout: Up to 6 hrs/month, 72 hours’ notice required, monthly calendar provided 30 days in advance, one change allowed per month.
  * Credits for incidents affecting batch routes: pro-rated by affected token counts; Redwood will provide a reconciliation CSV within 10 business days of month-end. Disputes to be raised within 30 days.

- Rationale: This gets us closer to Skyline’s request while protecting Redwood from open-ended exposure and giving us a clear measurement/reconciliation path.

Next step: If Skyline is comfortable with the 99.7% batch SLO and the 10% Dedicated cap, I’ll share an SLA redline (DocuSign-ready) by EOD Wednesday. If you prefer a lower cap, let me know and I’ll include optional language for a separate commercial addendum.

Thanks — looking forward to wrapping this up.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
